So each non-first host's Office365 service posts to the first host's externalId with its own token — exactly as the finding describes. CalendarManager's catch returning undefined on 404 would silently swallow it. Verified as a real defect.

judged_text: createEvent builds the events URL from only the first destination calendar (`mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId`), ignoring the per-credential destination and the credentialId argument the new Calendar interface passes. For a collective booking with multiple Office365 hosts, each non-first host's createEvent call posts to `/me/calendars/{firstHostExternalId}/events` with that host's own token; Graph returns 404/ErrorItemNotFound, CalendarManager's catch swallows it, and only the first host's Office365 calendar ever receives the event while the booking reference still records the wrong externalCalendarId.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `destinationCalendar` an array and updates the Calendar interface to `createEvent(event, credentialId)`, but `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` still derives the Graph URL from only the first element: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` then uses `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` to build `/me/calendars/{...}/events`. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, collective bookings can push multiple destination calendars into `evt.destinationCalendar` and then call `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` per destination. However `CalendarManager.createEvent` passes only `credential.id` into `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` (not the per-destination externalId), so Office365 cannot select the matching calendar and will keep using the first destination calendar externalId regardless of which credential/token is used. That can cause per-host Office365 inserts to target the wrong calendarId and fail (404), and `CalendarManager`’s catch explicitly swallows 404s (returns `undefined`), leading to only the first host succeeding while references can still carry `result.externalId` from the intended destination.
